channel.title: The Brussels Times
channel.description: Latest posts from The Brussels Times.

item.title: 'Deceptive sales to children': Сlass-action lawsuit filed in the Netherlands against Fortnite
item.description: Fortnite is especially popular with younger audiences, in Belgium too.

item.title: Europe lost up to €113 billion this year due to extreme heat
item.description: Italy is expected to suffer the biggest hit to its GDP, followed by Germany and France.

item.title: US judge orders to restore White House press access, despite Trump's ban
item.description: The ruling is temporary and will remain in force for two weeks.

item.title: French mosque dedicates sermon to Pope Leo XIV's visit
item.description: The Grand Mosque of Paris will devote its Friday sermon to Pope Leo XIV’s visit to France and relations between Christians and Muslims, its rector says.

item.title: Zelenskyy denounces Putin's 'madness' in his address to the UN
item.description: Ukraine's President draws attention to the fate of tens of thousands of soldiers from 47 countries sent to fight alongside Russian troops.

item.title: Belgian passport drops two spots in global ranking for visa-free destinations
item.description: Out of the 199 surveyed destinations, Belgians require a visa in advance for just 25 countries.

item.title: Polish army reports short airspace violation by Russian army helicopter
item.description: Polish army had to scramble fighter jets and put ground troops on alert.

item.title: Denmark, Greenland and US sign security agreement
item.description: 'The agreement recognizes the sovereignty and territorial integrity of our Kingdom [Denmark] and the Greenlandic people's right to self-determination.'

item.title: Macron asks for relaxation of EU rules to curb fuel prices
item.description: He also argued for more flexible rules on blending biofuels, saying this would create “additional room for supply”.

item.title: No agreement on extending Russian sanctions as EU deadline approaches
item.description: European Union member states have still not reached agreement on renewing sanctions against around 3,000 Russian individuals and organisations.

item.title: Infantino proposes reforms to the FIFA Executive Committee
item.description: Infantino has proposed a reform to the organisation's governing body after he was forced to withdraw a proposed sale of the media rights for the World Cup

item.title: Macron has meeting with Trump on Ukraine and Middle East: 'Very constructive talk'
item.description: French President Emmanuel Macron has held a bilateral meeting with his American counterpart, Donald Trump, ahead of the United Nations' annual meeting.

item.title: USA: Hundreds of flights scrapped due to technical glitch
item.description: By about 20:00 BST, Newark Airport had recorded 168 cancellations and 97 delays, according to flight tracking website FlightAware.

item.title: All far-right protesters released in The Hague following violent riots
item.description: Most of those detained were released on Saturday, while the remaining suspects were freed on Sunday.

item.title: Belgian minister can't visit New York UN Assembly due to oxygen tank prohibition on plane
item.description: According to her office, transporting the cylinder on flights to the United States is prohibited and no exception could be made in this case.

item.title: Far-right demonstration in the Hague infiltrated by neo-Nazis leaves city in shock and shame
item.description: “It's important that this is dealt with very harshly. Hitler salutes, antisemitic slogans, violence against the police, and throwing fireworks at the riot police."

item.title: Extinction Rebellion climate activists block Dutch highway to Germany
item.description: Earlier, police had kept between 100 and 200 demonstrators away from the A12, but a smaller group later managed to reach the road.

item.title: Far-right demonstration turns into rioting and clashes with police in The Hague
item.description: Anti-Semitic slogans were shouted, including “Hamas, Hamas, Jews to the gas”.

item.title: Denmark to sign security agreement with US on Greenland after all
item.description: Foreign minister Lars Løkke Rasmussen said next week could be “a good week” for Greenland, Denmark and the United States.

item.title: Luxembourg airport suspends flights due to drone activity, including to Brussels
item.description: It said 17 inbound flights were diverted to other airports, including Brussels, Paris and Frankfurt.
